title: Satchakranirupanacitram (Illustrated Six Chakras)
shelf_note: An illustrated book of chakra plates with Devanagari and English labels. It fits a Sanskrit/tantric-yoga reading, but the record has no tradition and no collections, so there is no shelf to test it against.
rights_flag: Undated 20th-century colour-printed plate with English anatomical labels (faint "EPIGASTRIC PLEXUS" at the top right). This looks like a modern printed chart book, so check its copyright status against the author's dates and the date of printing.
structure_note: The structure counts say pages_translated 0, but book.pages_translated and pages_translated_field say 63, and this page has a translation; the counters disagree (E2). Only 32 of 63 pages carry a printed number, with 6 backsteps and 4 repeats. In a book of plates, that more likely comes from misread or plate numerals than from a scan splice, but one page cannot settle it.

pages.layout: full-page colour plate: a faint blue-grey lotus (about ten petals) around a large tan seed syllable with chandrabindu, two white seated figures inside its loop; faint Devanagari/English labels at the top and a ruled multi-column table at the foot; heavy show-through

ocr_errors.image: The faint heading block at the top right carries the English label "EPIGASTRIC PLEXUS" (the solar plexus, i.e. Manipura), not the throat chakra. The Devanagari heading above it is too faint to read, but nothing supports Vishuddha.

ocr_errors.image: The large syllable is र with chandrabindu (headline, short stem, loop to the right, diagonal tail down-left, the ₹-like form): रँ/रं (raṃ), Manipura's seed syllable
ocr_errors.problem: Seed syllable misread as Haṃ, the expected bija for Vishuddha

ocr_errors.image: The foot table is too faint to read at this resolution. The cells cannot be Vishuddha's attributes (space, Sadashiva, Shakini) if the plate is Manipura (fire, Rudra/Vishnu, Lakini).

book_verdict: The plate shows Manipura: the seed syllable is रं, there are about ten petals, and it is labelled "EPIGASTRIC PLEXUS". The transcription and translation call it Vishuddha with Haṃ, Sadashiva, Shakini and space, and fill the illegible table with the expected attributes. Confident notes then present that misreading as fact, so an expert would flag it on sight.
